description: Overview of all nodes, services, power, network, AI usage, and storage across the home LAN.

panels.description: One row per host running node-exporter, joined on instance: kernel and release, CPU and memory utilisation, core count, total RAM, uptime, and wifi signal where the host is wireless. Hosts that stop reporting drop out of the table -- the Service Health tiles below are what tells you a node is down.

targets.expr:
max by (instance) (node_uname_info{job="node", sysname="Linux", release!~".*(microsoft|WSL).*"})
or
  max by (instance) (node_uname_info{job="node", sysname="Linux", release=~".*(microsoft|WSL).*"}) * 2
or
  max by (instance) (node_uname_info{job="node", sysname="Darwin"}) * 3
or
  max by (instance) (windows_os_info) * 4

panels.title: Node Fleet

panels.description: Every AMD GPU on the LAN, detected from node_exporter's hwmon collector rather than from the vendor exporter. hwmon reports an amdgpu chip whenever the kernel driver is bound, so a card shows up here even if amd-gpu-metrics-exporter is down or serving an empty registry. Read the two together: a row with a PCI chip but Exporter DOWN is an exporter fault; Exporter UP with no PCI chip means the driver never bound (check for a blacklist in /etc/modprobe.d). GPU, Busy % and vendor power come from the exporter, so they stay blank until it is healthy.

targets.expr: max by (server_name) (amd_gpu_average_package_power) or max by (server_name) ((node_hwmon_power_watt or node_hwmon_power_average_watt) and on (instance, chip) node_hwmon_chip_names{chip_name="amdgpu"})

panels.title: GPU Inventory

panels.description: How many node-exporter targets are currently up. There are eight in the scrape config, so anything below that is a host that is off or unreachable.
panels.title: Node Exporter

panels.description: Lemonade instances reporting themselves up. Counts lemonade_server_up rather than scrape state, so a running-but-wedged server still shows here.
panels.title: Lemonade

panels.description: How many nvme-exporter targets are up.
panels.title: NVMe Exporter

panels.description: Count of amd-gpu-metrics-exporter targets that are up, across all hosts.
panels.title: GPU Exporter

panels.description: Whether the speedtest exporter on the beelink is being scraped successfully.
panels.title: Speedtest

panels.description: Whether the Emporia smart-plug exporter is being scraped successfully.
panels.title: Emporia

panels.description: Scrape state of the iCloud exporter on localhost:9948. It has been refusing connections since the exporter stopped; the dashboard that consumed its metrics was retired on 2026-09-03. The tile stays because the job is still in the scrape config.
panels.title: iCloud

panels.description: Scrape state of the Cursor exporter. Note that up=1 here is not the same as working: the exporter answers scrapes but its Cursor API calls fail, so it emits only the cursor_subscription_* gauges. Its dashboard was retired on 2026-09-03 for that reason.
panels.title: Cursor

panels.description: Scrape state of the OpenAI exporter. As with Cursor, up=1 overstates its health -- it serves only Go runtime metrics, no openai_* series at all, so the daily-cost panel that used to sit under AI & Developer Usage was removed.
panels.title: OpenAI

panels.description: Prometheus scraping itself. This needs metrics_path: /prometheus/metrics in the scrape config, because the server runs behind --web.route-prefix=/prometheus and a bare /metrics returns 404.
panels.title: Prometheus

panels.description: How many hsa-snoop targets are up.
panels.title: HSA Snoop

panels.description: Instantaneous draw across all eight Emporia plugs. Each term is wrapped in "or vector(0)" so a plug that drops out of the scrape contributes zero rather than voiding the whole sum.

targets.expr: sum(snoc_pinewood_plug_a_power or vector(0)) + sum(snoc_pinewood_plug_b_power or vector(0)) + sum(snoc_pinewood_plug_c_power or vector(0)) + sum(snoc_pinewood_plug_d_power or vector(0)) + sum(snoc_pinewood_plug_e_power or vector(0)) + sum(snoc_pinewood_plug_f_power or vector(0)) + sum(snoc_pinewood_plug_g_power or vector(0)) + sum(snoc_pinewood_plug_h_power or vector(0))

panels.title: Total Home Power

panels.description: Per-plug draw over time. See the Emporia SmartPlugs dashboard for which plug is which and for on/off state.
panels.title: Power by Plug

panels.description: Download throughput from the most recent speedtest run, converted from the exporter's bytes/s to bits/s.
panels.title: WAN Download

panels.description: Upload throughput from the same run, likewise in bits/s.
panels.title: WAN Upload

panels.description: Idle latency and jitter from the speedtest run. The jitter series uses speedtest_jittter_seconds -- the exporter's own misspelling, not a typo here.
panels.title: WAN Latency & Jitter

panels.description: WiFi signal strength per node. Closer to 0 is better.
panels.title: WiFi Signal Strength

panels.description: Time to first token per Lemonade server node.
panels.title: Lemonade TTFT

panels.description: Token generation rate per Lemonade server node.
panels.title: Lemonade Tokens/s

panels.description: Every NVMe drive across the fleet, joined by instance: spare capacity, composite temperature, power-on hours and lifetime media errors. Media Errors turns red at 1 -- it should never leave zero.
panels.title: NVMe Health

panels.description: Space used on every ext4, xfs and btrfs mount. tmpfs and the like are excluded deliberately.
panels.title: Filesystem Usage

panels.description: 1-minute load average per node. Values above core count indicate overload.
panels.title: 1-Minute Load Average

panels.description: Memory usage percentage per node.
panels.title: Memory Usage %
